papers.title: Semilinear elliptic eigenvalue problem: Parametric analyticity and the uncertainty quantification
papers.abstract: In this paper, to the best of our knowledge, we make the first attempt at studying the parametric semilinear elliptic eigenvalue problems with the parametric coefficient and some power-type nonlinearities. The parametric coefficient is assumed to have an affine dependence on the countably many parameters with an appropriate class of sequences of functions. In this paper, we obtain the upper bound estimation for the mixed derivatives of the ground eigenpairs that has the same form obtained recently for the linear eigenvalue problem. The three most essential ingredients for this estimation are the parametric analyticity of the ground eigenpairs, the uniform boundedness of the ground eigenpairs, and the uniform positive differences between ground eigenvalues of linear operators. All these three ingredients need new techniques and a careful investigation of the nonlinear eigenvalue problem that will be presented in this paper. As an application, considering each parameter as a uniformly distributed random variable, we estimate the expectation of the eigenpairs using a randomly shifted quasi-Monte Carlo lattice rule and show the dimension-independent error bound.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文纯粹是数学理论分析，与有限元代理模型和植入物设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: It does not address FEA surrogate modeling, constraint handling, or practical biomechanics design; it is a pure mathematical analysis of eigenvalue problems.

summary_zh.motivation: 首次研究参数化半线性椭圆特征值问题的解析性和不确定性量化。
summary_zh.method: 推导了特征对的混合导数上界估计，并结合随机平移拟蒙特卡洛方法。
summary_zh.result: 得到了维数无关的误差界，证明了特征对的参数解析性。
summary_zh.validation: 理论证明上界估计和误差界，无数值实验。

summary_en.motivation: This paper makes the first attempt to study parametric semilinear elliptic eigenvalue problems with parametric coefficients and power-type nonlinearities.
summary_en.method: Upper bounds for mixed derivatives of ground eigenpairs are derived using parametric analyticity, uniform boundedness, and positive eigenvalue gaps, followed by quasi-Monte Carlo integration.
summary_en.result: Dimension-independent error bounds for expectation estimation of eigenpairs are established.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical proofs of analyticity and error bounds are provided, without numerical experiments.

papers.title: Learning-Rate-Free Learning: Dissecting D-Adaptation and Probabilistic Line Search
papers.abstract: This paper explores two recent methods for learning rate optimisation in stochastic gradient descent: D-Adaptation (arXiv:2301.07733) and probabilistic line search (arXiv:1502.02846). These approaches aim to alleviate the burden of selecting an initial learning rate by incorporating distance metrics and Gaussian process posterior estimates, respectively. In this report, I provide an intuitive overview of both methods, discuss their shared design goals, and devise scope for merging the two algorithms.

llm.why_not_core: This paper discusses learning rate optimization for SGD, with no connection to FEA surrogate modeling, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanical design.

papers.title: Randomized Neural Networks with Petrov-Galerkin Methods for Solving Linear Elasticity Problems
papers.abstract: We develop the Randomized Neural Networks with Petrov-Galerkin Methods (RNN-PG methods) to solve linear elasticity problems. RNN-PG methods use Petrov-Galerkin variational framework, where the solution is approximated by randomized neural networks and the test functions are piecewise polynomials. Unlike conventional neural networks, the parameters of the hidden layers of the randomized neural networks are fixed randomly, while the parameters of the output layer are determined by the least square method, which can effectively approximate the solution. We also develop mixed RNN-PG methods for linear elasticity problems, which ensure the symmetry of the stress tensor and avoid locking effects. We compare RNN-PG methods with the finite element method, the mixed discontinuous Galerkin method, and the physics-informed neural network on several examples, and the numerical results demonstrate that RNN-PG methods achieve higher accuracy and efficiency.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not include uncertainty quantification, implant-specific geometry or boundary conditions, nor any experimental or clinical validation for biomedical applications.

summary_en.motivation: To develop an efficient and accurate numerical solver for linear elasticity problems using randomized neural networks.
summary_en.method: The method integrates randomized neural networks with a Petrov-Galerkin variational framework, where hidden-layer weights are fixed randomly and output-layer weights are solved via least squares.
summary_en.result: Numerical experiments demonstrate superior accuracy and efficiency compared to finite element, mixed discontinuous Galerkin, and physics-informed neural network methods.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on benchmark elasticity problems with comparisons to established numerical methods.

papers.title: Improving the Mechanical Properties of a Lattice Structure Composed of Struts with a Tri-Directional Elliptical Cylindrical Section via Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: In recent years, lattice structures produced via additive manufacturing have been increasingly investigated for their unique mechanical properties and the flexible and diverse approaches available to design them. The design of a strut with variable cross-sections in a lattice structure is required to improve the mechanical properties. In this study, a lattice structure design method based on a strut cross-section composed of a mixture of three ellipses named a tri-directional elliptical cylindrical section (TEC) is proposed. The lattice structures were fabricated via the selective laser melting of 316L alloy. The finite element analysis results show that the TEC strut possessed the high mechanical properties of lattice structures. Compression experiments confirmed that the novel lattice structure with the TEC strut exhibited increases in the elastic modulus, compressive yield strength, and energy absorption capacity of 24.99%, 21.66%, and 20.50%, respectively, compared with the conventional lattice structure at an equal level of porosity.

papers.title: Regional specific tunable meniscus decellularized extracellular matrix (MdECM) reinforced bioink promotes anistropic meniscus regeneration
papers.abstract: The healing of meniscus injuries poses a significant challenge, as prolonged failure to heal can lead to osteoarthritis, which presents a therapeutic dilemma in the field of sports medicine. Decellularized extracellular matrix (MdECM) derived from natural meniscus, and the incorporated growth factors have been used for potential fibrochondrocyte induction and meniscus regeneration. However, homogeneous MdECM is difficult to achieve region-specific biomimetic microenvironment for tissue regeneration. In this study, we successfully prepared a region-specific MdECM, which were then mixed with an ultraviolet responsible Gelatin Methacryloyl (GelMA)/hyaluronic acid Methacryloy (HAMA) hydrogel incorporated with bioactive factors, faciliatated a functional region-specific bioink. The 3D printed scaffold by anistropic MdECM and zonally designed microstructure could promote chondrogenic differentiation of inner region cells and fibrochondrogenic differentiation of outer zone cell, ultimately enhanced anisotropic meniscus regeneration and cartilage protection.

summary_en.motivation: To achieve a region-specific biomimetic microenvironment for anisotropic meniscus regeneration.
summary_en.method: A region-specific decellularized meniscus extracellular matrix (MdECM) was prepared and combined with GelMA/HAMA hydrogel to formulate a functional bioink for 3D printing.
